fichas.title: Communal Storerooms for Bicycles and Prams
fichas.summary: Communal storerooms are required for prams, pushchairs and bicycles in residential building classes 3–5, and should also be provided in other residential buildings and detached houses. Plan for at least one vehicle per occupant, including children, and allow for mopeds, tricycles and trailers. Rooms should preferably be at street level, lockable, and fitted with hooks and bicycle stands. They may be inside the building with access to the entrance or in separate bicycle sheds; provide additional outdoor bicycle stands, especially when the storeroom is in the cellar. The illustrated bicycle/pram room is an example for about 20 vehicles.
fichas.building_type: Residential buildings; communal bicycle and pram storeroom
uses: Store bicycles, prams, pushchairs, bicycle trailers, tricycles and mopeds

ROOMS
Subsidiary Rooms

Communal storerooms
In addition to the storerooms or storage spaces in each flat,
for residential buildings in building classes 3-5, the building
regulations require an easily accessible (communal) storeroom
for prams, pushchairs and bicycles. Corresponding areas should
also be provided in other residential buildings and detached
houses.

For the design of these rooms, it can be assumed that at
least one vehicle per occupant (including children) has to be
accommodated. In addition to bicycles, prams and pushchairs,
it is also necessary to consider mopeds, tricycles, trailers etc.

-->0.

Living areas

The rooms should if possible be located at street level, be lockable
and equipped with hooks and bicycle stands to secure the stored
vehicles. They can be laid out as storerooms inside the building (with
access to the entrance) or as separate bicycle sheds --> f) - 8.
A sufficient number of additional bicycle stands should be provided
in the open air, particularly if the storeroom has been situated in the
cellar.
Cellar
The storage space provided for each flat normally consists of
a storeroom inside the flat --> p. 162, and an additional space
outside the flat. This is normally provided as a cellar compartment
--> 0but can also be provided inexpensively as a parking shed
in the grounds. Cellar storerooms should be dry and well ventilated.
Natural lighting is to be recommended. Appropriate detailing of the
window opening can optimise the light entering --> 0.

0 Space required for bicycles, prams, pushchairs, bicycle trailers, tricycles,
mopeds etc.

fichas.title: Cellar Compartment in a Residential Building
fichas.summary: Storage for each flat normally includes an in-flat storeroom and additional storage outside the flat, usually as a cellar compartment. An inexpensive alternative is a parking shed in the grounds. Cellar storerooms should be dry and well ventilated; natural lighting is recommended, and careful detailing of the window opening can improve light entry. The illustrated cellar compartment includes a light shaft and steel shelf.
uses: Store household belongings outside the flat
Provide natural light and ventilation to storage space
